root_cause.text: In the shmem truncation path, when a large swap entry is found at a non-aligned index (middle of the entry), the retry logic reuses the same index instead of rounding down to the entry's base, causing an infinite loop because the same entry is repeatedly encountered.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "When `index` points to the middle of a large swap entry... the code will then call shmem_confirm_swap(), get the order, check if it crosses the END boundary (which it doesn't), and retry with the same index. The next iteration will find the same entry again at the same index with same indices, leading to an infinite loop." The patch fixes this by changing the retry index to `round_down(base, 1 << order)` (i.e., the entry's base) and adding a check for start border to abort if the base is outside the truncate range.
